bibliographic.title: Optimizing Large Language Models for ESG Activity Detection in Financial Texts
bibliographic.authors: Mattia Birti; Andrea Maurino; Francesco Osborne
bibliographic.venue: 6th ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF '25)
bibliographic.citation_apa: Birti, M., Maurino, A., & Osborne, F. (2025). Optimizing Large Language Models for ESG Activity Detection in Financial Texts. In Proceedings of the 6th ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF '25) (pp. 1-8). ACM. https://doi.org/10.1145/3768292.3770371

methodology.method_family: benchmark dataset creation and supervised fine-tuning evaluation
methodology.study_design: experimental comparison of LLMs for domain-specific text classification
methodology.sample_description: ESG-Activities benchmark with labeled text segments from financial/sustainability disclosures classified according to the EU ESG taxonomy
methodology.technology_context: fine-tuned open and proprietary LLMs for ESG environmental-activity text classification in financial texts; not a conversational or agentic system

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article empirically optimizes LLMs for ESG activity detection in financial texts via fine-tuning and benchmark evaluation. It does not study conversational AI systems, chatbots, agents, RAG pipelines, guardrails, observability, human oversight, accountability mechanisms, or governance of LLM-based conversational deployments in regulated settings.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper uses LLMs in a regulated financial/compliance context and mentions ESG regulatory frameworks, its core contribution is technical text classification and dataset benchmarking. No conversational interface, dialogue governance, operational oversight, audit/logging, or conversational risk controls are addressed. Python conversational_ai score was 0/3, consistent with the provided text.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Scope mismatch is explicit in title, abstract, and stated task definition; exclusion does not depend on ambiguous governance terminology.

appraisal.notes: Methodological quality appears adequate for an empirical NLP classification study, but appraisal relevance to conversational governance in regulated LLM systems is very low. Full methodology and evaluation details are only partially visible in the excerpt provided.

cerqual.explanation: For the review question on conversational governance of LLM systems in regulated environments, the study is only weakly relevant despite financial/compliance context. It offers limited transferable evidence on governance mechanisms, oversight, or conversational risk management.

coding.theme: Domain-specific LLM optimization for financial ESG classification
coding.subtheme: Benchmarking and fine-tuning for environmental-activity detection
rq_alignment: weak alignment: regulated financial context with LLMs
no alignment: human oversight or accountability in conversational systems

synthesis.main_claim: Current-generation LLMs can identify environmental-activity-related text in financial disclosures, and fine-tuning on the authors' ESG-Activities benchmark substantially improves classification performance over general-purpose models.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces the ESG-Activities benchmark with 1,325 labeled segments and shows that fine-tuned open models can outperform some proprietary LLMs for EU ESG taxonomy-aligned environmental activity detection.
synthesis.limitations: General-purpose LLMs are limited in domain-specific ESG activity categorization; high-quality structured training data are scarce; task is more complex than broad SDG linking.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance. May serve only as distant contextual background on regulated-finance NLP uses of LLMs, not on governance of conversational LLM systems.
